# A Tour of the Beast Pens

*Page PDF 105*

The Scalefl ayer Menagerie 

## **A Tour of the Beast Pens**
Despite Scaleflayer’s misgivings, privileged Druchii on _Temple of Spite_ sometimes tour the pens, to ogle the more exotic or impressive creatures, throw them a captive or two, and generally amuse themselves. 

## **The Menagerie and Stables**
The upper Beast Pens are where the beastmasters reside in sparse chambers. Nearby are stables, home to the black ark’s dark steeds. These horses fare better amidst the cold stone than any regular steed, used as they are to Naggaroth’s climate. Even so, they are fed a stupefying concoction to keep them docile over long voyages. 

The Menagerie contains many creatures meant as curiosities, potential status symbols should they reach Clar Karond, and these are the most interesting part of the beast pens for a lay elf. A culchan, Lustria’s famed predatory bird, hisses warnings at passersby, while cages of brightly-coloured macaws cry out in near-human voices, and doomwings skulk on their perches or tear at meat thrown to them by a beastmaster. A war lion of Chrace huddles in its cage, white fur crisscrossed with scars. The collection’s current pride is a tiger-headed beastman, captured in Ind. Scaleflayer hopes this creature might serve in Clar Karond’s fighting pits, though for now it refuses to move. 

## **Captive Cells**
A person wandering through the cells may see humans, elves, orcs, dwarfs, beastmen, all cramped together in iron-barred chambers. Fights between captives are common and are encouraged by their overseers, the whelpmasters. There is little glory in this role and many take bribes from Druchii looking to secure themselves choice captives or hobble one due to fight in the amphitheatre. Gharin Redscowl organises unofficial pit fights in the cells, where the black ark’s dregs come to prove their devotion to Khaine against a captive. 

Next to the cells are the kennels, where the warhounds reside. Dark elves cultivate a vicious breed of black-furred dog, cowed into submission by the brutality of their handlers. The incessant barking adds to the fear felt by captives. 

## **Kharibdyss Enclosure**
The beastmasters keep a section of their domain flooded. Here, a beastmaster may walk along dripping, damp corridors and peer through glass apertures in the rock wall, sorcerously enhanced to keep the water, and Scorath’s prized kharibdyss, contained. This has not stopped the creature from attacking the glass when it senses someone passing. Sometimes, the kharibdyss disappears, and the beastmasters content themselves it is merely resting beyond their sight in some corner of its enclosure. In fact, the creature has scratched a fissure in the wall allowing access to an adjoining tunnel leading to long-abandoned caverns in the depths of the ark, where it ventures out to hunt. 

## **Cold Ones Corral**
Cold ones are so vicious they cannot be stabled near other creatures and, instead, have their own broad, dark chamber, mimicking Naggaroth’s dank caverns, save for unlit braziers strung throughout. Their food is lowered in through openings in the ceiling, unbound to give the cold ones exercise as they chase it down. When the beastmasters venture inside, they must first petition Beastmaster Kelrathi. She keeps her study nearby, being one of the few who can stand the cold ones’ stench. Here lies the master brazier. Once this is lit, all the others within the enclosure burst into flames, burning a secret, sickly concoction which emits thick smoke. This dissipates quickly, but renders the cold ones sluggish. Should an elf breathe it in, they may never regain their wits. 

## **Hydra Pits**
Deep pits, criss-crossed with walkways, mark the war hydras’ lair. The vicious monsters are forever ravenous and so are kept close to the cells, ensuring at least one food source is always nearby. The screams of unfortunate victims, chosen each week from among the captives, are an eternal reminder of what awaits those who fall from the beastmasters’ favour.
